candidates.summary: The fix also changes the result of four loop shapes that compile on master, so deployed realms using them switch behaviour at the upgrade, yet the PR says the shapes were rejected and there is no gas change
candidates.failure_scenario: On master, when a plain variable with the loop variable's name is in scope, the four shapes do not fail. They bind the plain variable and report success. `x := 100; for x := 1; x < 3; x++ { for x := range make([]int, x) {...} }` iterates 0..99 twice (200 lines) on master and 0, 0, 1 at head. `var x any = "outer"; for x := any(1); ...; { switch x := x.(type) }` prints `other outer` on master and `int 1` at head. `k := -1; for k := 0; k < 1; k++ { for k = range []int{7,8} {}; println(k) }; println(k)` prints `0 1` on master (the range writes the outer k) and `1 -1` at head. The `x := 5; for x := x; ...` case inside `for x := 0` prints 0..6 on master and 5 6 at head. go/types accepts all four, so addpkg could deploy them under the old binary. gno.land never persists BlockNodes (store.go:162-163) and re-preprocesses every stored package at boot (keeper.go:203, PreprocessAllFilesAndSaveBlockNodes). A realm deployed with one of these shapes therefore runs a different loop count, with different gas and different state writes, from the first block on the new binary. A validator or RPC node still on the old binary keeps computing and serving the old result for the same transaction or query until it upgrades. The PR body says these shapes are 'valid Go rejected on master' and claims 'No gas change'. A reader classifying this as a change with no consensus impact would miss this.

candidates.summary: The second initStaticBlocks pass is not allocation-free as the PR says: every FuncDecl and FuncLitExpr still allocates a frame map on each pass
candidates.failure_scenario: The PR body says the second initStaticBlocks pass 'is now allocation-free'. The ADR says it 'allocates none at all'. But the FuncDecl and FuncLitExpr cases call pushClone with a non-nil, delete-only modify. Because `modify == nil && len(parent) == 0` is false, the fast path is skipped and `f := map[Name]bool{}` is allocated for every function and every function literal in the file, on both passes, even though deleting from an empty parent frame changes nothing. The cost is small but grows with the number of functions. The fix is to let a delete-only push take the fast path when the parent frame is empty.
candidates.verify_by: Read preprocess.go pushClone (fast path at `if modify == nil && len(parent) == 0`) and the FuncLitExpr/FuncDecl ENTER cases (pushClone(func(f){delete...})); a Go test that runs initStaticBlocks1 twice on a file with N funcs and wraps the second run in testing.AllocsPerRun shows allocations that grow with N
